accepted.s: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY), launched in November 2015, was primarily intended for which of the following purposes?
o: Financial turnaround and revival of DISCOMs
Universal installation of nuclear power plants
Privatisation of all State Electricity Boards
accepted.x: UDAY was launched in November 2015 to achieve the financial turnaround and revival of distribution companies.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the purpose associated with the named scheme.
accepted.sec: UDAY - purpose, debt takeover, operational and demand-side interventions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to UDAY, consider the following statements:
1. States took over 75% of DISCOM debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015.
2. Fifty per cent of the debt was taken over in 2015-16 and 25% in 2016-17.
3. The arrangement covered 97% of the total outstanding DISCOM debt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. UDAY provided for State takeover of 75% of DISCOM debt in the two specified instalments, covering 97% of total outstanding debt.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: UDAY - purpose, debt takeover, operational and demand-side interventions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a demand-side intervention under UDAY?
accepted.x: The use of energy-efficient LED bulbs is a demand-side intervention. Coal swapping, transformer upgrades and feeder metering are operational interventions.
accepted.tq: Separate operational measures from measures that reduce consumer-side energy demand.
accepted.sec: UDAY - purpose, debt takeover, operational and demand-side interventions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) was conveyed on 3 December 2014. Which one of the following correctly describes it?
o: A scheme exclusively for nuclear-power generation
A scheme for last-mile household connections in urban areas only
A rural power scheme that subsumed RGGVY and aimed at 24x7 power in rural India
A scheme for privatisation of rural DISCOMs
accepted.x: DDUGJY was conveyed on 3 December 2014, subsumed the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana and aimed at providing 24x7 power in rural India.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, predecessor scheme and principal objective of a government programme.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for DDUGJY?
accepted.x: Rural Electrification Corporation, or REC, is the nodal agency for DDUGJY.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-association approach to identify the nodal agency.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following components of DDUGJY:
1. Separation of agricultural and non-agricultural feeders
2. Strengthening of sub-transmission and distribution systems
3. Development of micro-grids and off-grid systems
4. Metering of distribution transformers, feeders and consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four are components of DDUGJY. The scheme also includes rural electrification as a major component.
accepted.tq: Test the completeness of a scheme by checking whether each listed component belongs to its design.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under DDUGJY, the normal grant component and the additional milestone-linked support are respectively:
accepted.x: DDUGJY provides a 60% grant and additional support of up to 15% linked to milestones. For special-category States, the corresponding figures are 85% and 5%.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired percentage structure and distinguish ordinary from special-category States.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Approximately how many households had been electrified under Saubhagya?
accepted.x: Approximately 2.86 crore households were electrified under Saubhagya.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close numerical alternatives by retaining the exact crore figure.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between feeder separation, RDSS and PM-KUSUM?
o: Feeder separation ended with DDUGJY and has no connection with later schemes.
Feeder separation continues under RDSS, and separated agricultural feeders are subsequently solarised under PM-KUSUM.
PM-KUSUM separates urban commercial feeders under RDSS.
RDSS replaced feeder separation with only off-grid micro-grids.
accepted.x: Feeder separation continues under RDSS, while separated agricultural feeders can subsequently be solarised under PM-KUSUM.
accepted.tq: Trace the policy sequence from an infrastructure intervention to its later application.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY and Saubhagya - feeder separation, household electrification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) was introduced in which year, and what is its stated total outlay?
accepted.x: RDSS was introduced in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3.03 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Match the programme year with its distinctive outlay figure.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following features characterises RDSS?
1. It is reform-based.
2. It is results-linked.
3. It has been extended by two years up to FY 2027-28.
4. REC and PFC are its nodal agencies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. RDSS is reform-based and results-linked, has been extended to FY 2027-28, and uses REC and PFC as nodal agencies.
accepted.tq: Use a four-part scheme profile rather than relying on its name alone.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The pan-India target under RDSS for AT&C losses and the ACS-ARR gap is respectively:
accepted.x: RDSS targets pan-India AT&C losses of 12–15% and seeks to reduce the ACS-ARR gap to zero.
accepted.tq: Keep the policy target distinct from the latest observed performance values.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Under RDSS, smart metering is implemented on which model, with priority given to which consumers?

1. TOTEX model under a public-private partnership framework
2. Government offices
3. Commercial consumers
4. Commercial and industrial consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: RDSS smart metering follows the TOTEX model under PPP, with priority for government offices and commercial and C&I consumers.
accepted.tq: Link the implementation model with the priority consumer categories.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the smart-metering figures under RDSS?
accepted.x: Approximately 4.7 crore smart meters had been installed, while 20.34 crore had been sanctioned under RDSS.
accepted.tq: Compare installed and sanctioned quantities without reversing their status.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the metering technology requirements under RDSS is correct?
o: One hundred per cent Indian HES and MDMS systems are mandated.
HES and MDMS are excluded from the scheme.
At least 50% Indian HES and MDMS systems are mandated.
Only imported HES and MDMS systems are permitted.
accepted.x: RDSS mandates 100% Indian HES and MDMS systems for the specified smart-metering programme.
accepted.tq: Watch for the exact percentage in a technology-procurement requirement.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What is the role of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) in the smart-metering context?
o: It replaces REC as the nodal agency of RDSS.
It certifies all nuclear power plants.
It acts as the regulator for electricity tariffs.
It undertakes demand aggregation for large smart-metering programmes.
accepted.x: EESL undertakes demand aggregation for large smart-metering programmes.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific operational role rather than confusing it with a regulatory or nodal role.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: EESL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with PNGRB for smart meters relating to:
accepted.x: EESL entered into an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters, where PNG means piped natural gas.
accepted.tq: Expand the abbreviation and match the organisation with the correct utility sector.
accepted.sec: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme - outlay, smart prepaid meters, EESL  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Rights of Consumers Rules, a new electricity connection is to be provided within which maximum periods in metropolitan, municipal and rural areas respectively?
accepted.x: The prescribed periods are 3 days in metropolitan areas, 7 days in municipal areas and 15 days in rural areas.
accepted.tq: Retain the geographical order while matching each area with its time limit.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Rights of Consumers Rules had been adopted by how many States and Union Territories?
accepted.x: The Rights of Consumers Rules had been adopted by all 36 States and Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total number of adopting units from the number of States alone.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Late Payment Surcharge Rules, 2022, legacy electricity dues were to be cleared through:
o: Waiver by the Central Electricity Authority
A single cash payment with penal interest
Conversion into equity of generating companies
accepted.x: The rules provided for clearance of legacy dues through interest-free equated monthly instalments.
accepted.tq: Identify the consumer-relief mechanism that follows from the rule’s purpose.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The dues payable to generating companies declined from approximately ₹1.35–1.39 lakh crore in 2022 to which amount in January 2026?
accepted.x: The dues fell to ₹4,927 crore by January 2026, representing an approximately 96% reduction from the 2022 level.
accepted.tq: Handle Indian-numbering figures carefully and avoid shifting a zero or decimal place.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The payment cycle for electricity-sector dues changed from 178 days in FY 2020-21 to how many days in FY 2024-25?
accepted.x: The payment cycle declined from 178 days in FY21 to 113 days in FY25.
accepted.tq: Compare the initial and latest values in the stated time sequence.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The amended Electricity Rules provide for automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes. What is the principal intended effect of this provision?
o: It prevents generating companies from changing fuel sources.
It prevents new deficits from arising due to unrecovered fuel-cost changes.
It abolishes all electricity tariffs for agricultural consumers.
It transfers all distribution losses to consumers without regulation.
accepted.x: Automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes is intended to prevent new deficits caused by delays in recovering such costs.
accepted.tq: Infer the financial consequence from the mechanism described in the rule.
accepted.sec: Electricity (Amendment) Bill and Rules - consumer rights, late payment surcharge  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: AT&C loss in the electricity sector refers to:
o: The difference between average cost and average revenue per unit
The unpaid subsidy released by the State Government
Technical and commercial losses, including theft, billing and collection inefficiency
Only technical losses in transmission lines
accepted.x: AT&C loss combines technical and commercial losses, including losses from theft, billing inefficiency and collection inefficiency.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a composite loss metric from the separate ACS-ARR financial gap.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap, PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: AT&C losses declined from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
accepted.x: AT&C losses declined to 15.04% in FY25 from 22.62% in FY14. The figure of 16.12% relates to FY24 in an older set of values.
accepted.tq: Match the exact percentage with the correct financial year and reject the nearby-year figure.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap, PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The ACS-ARR gap is defined as:
o: Average cost of supply minus average revenue realised per unit
Average revenue realised minus average cost of supply per consumer
Average subsidy received minus total generation cost
Annual commercial loss minus annual technical loss
accepted.x: ACS-ARR gap means average cost of supply minus average revenue realised per unit.
accepted.tq: Expand both components of the abbreviation and preserve their order in the subtraction.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap and PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The ACS-ARR gap decreased from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
accepted.x: The ACS-ARR gap fell to ₹0.06 per kWh in FY25 from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY14. This equals 6 paise per unit, not 0.06 paise.
accepted.tq: Check both the unit and the decimal placement in a small financial figure.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap and PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the financial performance of DISCOMs?
o: They posted a profit of ₹67,962 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹2,701 crore in 2013-14.
They posted identical profits in both years.
They posted a loss of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a profit of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
They posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
accepted.x: DISCOMs posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25, compared with a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
accepted.tq: Track both the direction of change and the year attached to each amount.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap and PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The PFC Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise grades DISCOMs annually on which basis?
o: Only the number of rural households connected
accepted.x: PFC annually grades DISCOMs on their financial and operational performance through its Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise.
accepted.tq: Identify the two-dimensional basis of the institutional rating.
accepted.sec: Loss metrics - AT&C, ACS-ARR gap and PFC rating  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Delhi DISCOMs — Privatised in 2002
2. Odisha DISCOMs — Taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21
3. Bhiwandi input-based franchise model — Torrent, 2007
4. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Recommendation for active DISCOM privatisation by States

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Delhi’s DISCOMs were privatised in 2002, Odisha’s were taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21, Bhiwandi pioneered the cited franchise model in 2007, and the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended active State-led privatisation.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure historical pair and verify the remaining institutional associations.
accepted.sec: Privatisation and franchise models  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The input-based franchisee model in electricity distribution was first implemented at Bhiwandi by:
accepted.x: The input-based franchisee model was first implemented at Bhiwandi by Torrent in 2007.
accepted.tq: Match the place, implementing entity and year in a reform-history question.
accepted.sec: Privatisation and franchise models  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh DISCOMs?
o: APSPDCL — Headquartered at Hyderabad after its 2020 re-formation
accepted.x: APSPDCL is headquartered at Tirupati. APCPDCL was re-formed in 2020 at Vijayawada; the older pre-2014 APCPDCL was associated with Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Find the single location and organisational-history mismatch.
accepted.sec: AP discoms - APSPDCL, APEPDCL, APCPDCL - losses, smart metering  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the change involving APSPDCL after bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It was re-formed at Vijayawada in 2020.
It took over all districts formerly served by APEPDCL.
It took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
accepted.x: At bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, APSPDCL took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific territorial transfer rather than the headquarters of the DISCOM.
accepted.sec: AP discoms - APSPDCL, APEPDCL, APCPDCL - losses, smart metering  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh DISCOMs:
1. Phase-2 smart meters were begun for industrial consumers.
2. APEPDCL and APSPDCL ranked among the top performers in loss reduction.
3. RDSS sanction for Andhra Pradesh was ₹15,083.14 crore.
4. APSPDCL had segregated 312 of 3,015 agricultural feeders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. They describe smart-metering, loss-reduction performance, RDSS sanction and agricultural-feeder segregation in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Verify each State-specific statistic and programme action independently.
accepted.sec: AP discoms - APSPDCL, APEPDCL, APCPDCL - losses, smart metering  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What proportion of APSPDCL’s agricultural feeders had been segregated, based on the reported figures of 312 out of 3,015?
accepted.x: 312 out of 3,015 is approximately 10.3%, or about 10%.
accepted.tq: Convert the reported numerator and denominator into an approximate percentage.
accepted.sec: AP discoms - APSPDCL, APEPDCL, APCPDCL - losses, smart metering  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The State stood guarantor for a ₹300 crore HUDCO loan obtained by which entity for rural distribution transformers?
accepted.x: The State stood guarantor for a ₹300 crore HUDCO loan to AP Power Finance Corporation for rural distribution transformers.
accepted.tq: Match the guarantor, lender, borrower and purpose in the financing arrangement.
accepted.sec: AP discoms - APSPDCL, APEPDCL, APCPDCL - losses, smart metering  [GROUP-II]
